description:
FILED s473q (Opus agent, 2026-09-07) while answering #1187.  Record:
docs/pcre2-spike-s473q.md Â§7.  MEASURED, NOT GUESSED - what is missing is a
decision about memory, not another number.

THE SITE.  The round-27 ranked table's rank-2 entry (`search`, 14.5% of json-rt
and 11.5% of textproc) is cl-ppcre/scanner.lisp:72

    (search pattern *string* :start2 start-pos :end2 *end-pos* :test test)

and that branch is taken ONLY when cl-ppcre:*use-bmh-matchers* is NIL.  It
defaults to NIL (cl-ppcre/specials.lisp:126) and PCL has never bound it.  T
switches literal-prefix scanning to a Boyer-Moore-Horspool matcher.

MEASURED (interleaved best-of-K, byte-identical control pair in the window,
quiet box):
  isolated literal-prefix scan     0.3090 s -> 0.0470 s   6.6x FASTER
  create-scanner x20 literal pats  ~0       -> 0.019 s    (~1 ms each)
  heap per literal pattern         0        -> 8.5 MB

  ROW LEVEL (scratch/s473q/ab-rt.pl against a runtime copy whose ONLY
  difference is the binding, scratch/s473q/mkrt-bmh.pl):
    row                default    BMH      ratio     peak RSS
    control(N=40000)   0.2912     0.2927   1.005     -
    textproc           1.9944     1.4813   0.743     91.6 -> 100.4 MB
    json-rt            2.6412     2.5662   0.972     94.9 ->  94.8 MB
    subste             0.2551     0.2539   0.995     75.2 ->  75.3 MB
    regexg             0.7530     0.7457   0.990     -
    pos100000/200000   0.1632/0.1564 -> 0.1570/0.1560  0.961 / 0.998

So it is a textproc-SHAPED lever: +34.6% on the one row whose patterns have
literal prefixes, ~0 elsewhere, for ONE extra skip table.  That clears the
20%-of-its-row bar comfortably.

WHY IT WAS NOT SHIPPED, AND WHAT THE DECISION IS.  The 8.5 MB is per LITERAL
PATTERN (only patterns with a constant start string build a BMH matcher), so a
real program pays it a handful of times - textproc paid it ONCE.  But it is
unbounded in principle: a module with 100 literal-prefix patterns would pay
850 MB.  The table's size is cl-ppcre:*regex-char-code-limit* = char-code-limit
= 1,114,112 fixnums, dense, and cl-ppcre's own docstring says lowering that
variable removes full Unicode support from character CLASSES - i.e. lowering it
to shrink the table is a silent-wrong generator, not an option.

THE SHAPES A FIX COULD TAKE (none of them measured; pick one and it is a small
change in %pcl-build-scanner):
  (a) a BUDGET: bind *use-bmh-matchers* to T while fewer than K literal-prefix
      scanners have been built.  Needs a K and an answer to "what happens to
      pattern K+1" (it silently gets the slow matcher, which is fine but must
      be said).
  (b) bind it only when the program's pattern COUNT is known small - PCL does
      not know that at scanner-build time.
  (c) upstream: a sparse/256-entry skip table with a fallback is the right fix
      and belongs in cl-ppcre, not here (CLAUDE.md 9a - and #71 would delete
      the whole question).
NOTE: if #71 is ever taken this task dies with it - PCRE2 has no such site.


=== FABLE RULING (s476, 2026-09-07, at the s473q merge) ===
DECISION: NOT the flag.  `*use-bmh-matchers*` = T is a dense table of *regex-char-code-limit* (1,114,112) fixnums per literal pattern -- unbounded across a module load, and the limit cannot be lowered (the same variable sizes the charclass maps).  The lever is REAL (+34.6 % textproc, the only row with literal prefixes) and it is the SHAPE of the table that is wrong, not the algorithm: Boyer-Moore-Horspool stays CORRECT with a HASHED skip table -- skip[h] = min over every char c with hash(c)=h of skip(c), default = needle length -- because a smaller skip is always safe (it can only under-skip, never past a match).  A 256-way table keyed on (logand code 255) costs 2 KB per pattern (vs 8.5 MB), is identical to the dense table for an ASCII/Latin-1 needle, and degrades gracefully for a non-Latin-1 one.
SHAPE, in order of preference, for the perf agent that takes it:
  (A) PCL supplies the matcher: shadow `cl-ppcre::create-bmh-matcher` (pattern case-insensitive-p) with the hashed version and bind `*use-bmh-matchers*` T at runtime load.  cl-ppcre is a Quicklisp system (asdf:load-system in the runtime, NOT vendored), so the redefinition is version-pinned: at load, assert the symbol is fbound in cl-ppcre with that lambda list, else REFUSE LOUDLY naming the cl-ppcre version (rule 12; the SBCL-internal-symbol precedent, `sb-impl::package-%use-list` s473r) -- never a silent fall-back to the generic `search`.
  (B) if (A) is not reachable (the matcher is inlined / the call site differs by version): PCL-side literal-prefix pre-scan in `%pcl-build-scanner` from PCL`s own knowledge of the pattern -- measure first; it duplicates cl-ppcre`s prefix extraction, which is why it is second.
BAR: textproc >= +30 % of its row (the measured lever is +34.6 %), json-rt/subste/regexg within the control spread, peak RSS FLAT (<= +1 MB on textproc; the flag reads +8.8 MB), a correctness probe over a needle set incl. a non-Latin-1 literal prefix and a case-insensitive one (`/foo/i` -> the case-folded table), the companion re/ leg before/after (`--jobs 1`), the full sweep (a `cl/` change), a Pl/t guard that fails on the base extraction (a pattern with a literal prefix over a long subject: the same answer as today AND the redefinition-present assertion).  Runtime-only, no gen bump.  Ease S-M.  Goes into the next perf brief (round 32) with the s473r fillers.


=== DONE (s473s, 2026-09-08) — shape (A), the hashed skip table ===

SHIPPED per the s476 FABLE RULING, shape (A): PCL supplies the MATCHER, not
merely the flag.  `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` gains `%pcl-bmh-skip-table` (256
fixnums keyed on `(logand (char-code c) 255)`, each bucket the MINIMUM skip
over every character in it), `%pcl-bmh-matcher-aux` (cl-ppcre's own
`bmh-matcher-aux` re-expressed with the hashed index), `%pcl-bmh-generic-
matcher` (cl-ppcre's no-BMH branch verbatim, so the replacement is a drop-in
for the WHOLE contract and a NIL flag still behaves as upstream),
`%pcl-create-bmh-matcher`, `%pcl-bmh-arglist`, `%pcl-bmh-decline` and
`%pcl-install-bmh-matcher`, which runs at runtime load.  Runtime-only: no
emission change, no generation bump.  Guard `Pl/t/bmh-scan-01.t` (6 rows,
inverse-verified: rows 1-3 fail on the base extraction).

CORRECTNESS.  BMH is correct under UNDER-skipping — the outer loop advances by
`(max 1 (aref skip …))`, so a skip smaller than the true one can only re-test
positions, never jump past a match — hence a hash bucket may safely take the
minimum over its colliding characters.  Verified three ways: 28 (pattern,
subject) cases give BYTE-IDENTICAL output under the generic `search`, under
cl-ppcre's own DENSE BMH and under the hashed one; a 16-row Perl program
(hits, misses, /i, a needle whose characters are all above Latin-1, a subject
holding characters that collide mod 256, a needle longer than the subject, an
empty match, //g over a 5 500-char subject, `split`, `s///g`) is identical to
perl 5.40.3; and the guard file re-runs both batteries.

SPEED (interleaved, all series in ONE window, best-of-9, column 2 a
byte-identical COPY of column 1 as the control, base = the batch's own HEAD,
`uptime` beside every reading, box at load 1.7-2.9):

  row        control   this change   dense (the flag alone)
  textproc    +2.9 %     -24.5 %       -24.5 %
  json-rt     +0.1 %      -1.4 %        --
  subste      +1.9 %      -0.3 %        --
  regexg      +1.1 %      +5.9 %        +3.9 %

textproc 1.9047 -> 1.4381 s = **+32.5 % faster**, clearing the +30 % bar, and
the hashed and dense columns are INDISTINGUISHABLE (1.4381 vs 1.4378) — the
256-way table costs nothing against the 8.5 MB one.  A first reading of
textproc on a contended box gave -19.3 % with the CONTROL at +14.0 %; it was
re-measured rather than quoted.

THE OTHER THREE ROWS CANNOT MOVE, which is why regexg's +5.9 % is noise and
not a regression: counting the matchers each row builds says textproc builds
exactly ONE (its `tag=t` literal prefix) while regexg, json-rt and subste
build ZERO.  (Every row reports one extra — the install self-test's own probe
scanner.)  A row that builds no BMH matcher runs the same code either way,
which is also why the dense column reads +3.9 % on regexg.

MEMORY, the reason the flag alone was refused: twenty literal-prefix scanners
take the heap 14.8 -> **184.8 MB** dense and 14.8 -> **14.9 MB** hashed; peak
RSS on `textproc` (best of 3) is base 99.9 MB, this change **98.2 MB**, the
flag alone 106.6 MB.  Flat, against a bar of <= +1 MB.  The guard asserts
under 2 MB of growth for those twenty scanners, so a regression to the dense
table cannot pass silently.

THE VERSION PIN IS TWO CHECKS, not one.  The lambda list is asserted
(`(PATTERN CASE-INSENSITIVE-P)`), but a lambda list cannot say whether
cl-ppcre still CALLS the fdefinition — and if a future version inlined or
block-compiled that call, the redefinition would be invisible while
`*use-bmh-matchers*` = T stayed in force, so cl-ppcre would allocate its own
8.5 MB table per pattern: strictly worse than doing nothing.  So the install
also SELF-TESTS, building a probe scanner for a literal prefix and keeping the
flag on only if the call is observed to arrive.  Either check failing leaves
scanning on the generic `search` (today's behaviour, identical answers) and
ANNOUNCES on stderr naming the cl-ppcre version — the rule-12 boundary (s329):
effect-only, so announce and continue, never silent.  Tested against
cl-ppcre 2.1.2.
subject: cl-ppcre:*use-bmh-matchers* is NIL by default and PCL never binds it: T reads textproc 0.743x (+34.6%) but costs 8.5 MB PER LITERAL PATTERN -- RULED s476: ship BMH with a 256-way HASHED skip table (2 KB/pattern; BMH stays correct under-skipping), shadowing create-bmh-matcher version-pinned with a loud refusal; bar textproc >= +30 %, RSS flat
